newsitem.title: USA: GM China venture could have 3,000 employees.
newsitem.headline: GM China venture could have 3,000 employees.

text.p: General Motor Corp's $1.57 billion automobile joint venture in Shanghai with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp could employ over 3,000 people when it reached full production, the company said.

The joint venture was formally announced on Tuesday, as a pact was signed at Beijing's Great Hall of the People by General Motors Chairman John Smith Jr and Shanghai Automotive Chairman Chen Xiang Lin.

The venture, to be held equally by General Motors and Shanghai Automotive, would be comprised of two entities - Shanghai GM, for the manufacture, sales and distribution of vehicles and Pan Asia Technical Automotive Center, for developing vehicle design and engineering, the companies said.

The Shanghai GM facility would include a vehicle assembly plant, a stamping plant, a V6 engine plant, an automatic transmission machining and assembly plant and vehicle marketing and distribution operations, it said.
Including manufacturing, purchasing, marketing, sales and distribution facilities, the new company could employ over 3,000 people, General Motors said.
General Motors said the 160,000 square meter assembly plant was scheduled to be completed by mid-1998.
Hiring for the new assembly plant would begin in the third quarter of 1997, the company said.
The Pan Asia Technical Automotive Center would ultimately employ over 300 engineers and technicians, it said.
Shanghai GM would begin building Buicks in late 1998, based on a new General Motors North American Operation Car Group platform, the company said.
The plant's production would reach 100,000 units, it said.
